task.title: PRODUCTDELETE
task.spec:
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants delete discontinued products all the time, and every time they do, something breaks. A cart that held the product can't be opened any more, and an order that included it can't be read by the merchant or by the customer who placed it.

Deleting a product (DELETE /api/v1/private/product/{id}) must not break carts or orders:

- Carts that held the product: GET /api/v1/cart/{code} returns the cart without it, with its subtotal, total and quantity worked out from the products left. A cart whose only product was deleted is returned with no products and a total of 0. The cart can still be changed (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}, POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi) and checked out; the deleted product is never ordered or charged. Trying to add the deleted product to a cart gives HTTP 404 Not Found.
- Orders that included the product: GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}, GET /api/v1/private/orders, GET /api/v1/auth/orders/{id} and GET /api/v1/auth/orders keep working, and show the product as it was bought: its sku, name, ordered quantity, price and subtotal, exactly as before it was deleted. The order's totals don't change. The order's status can still be changed (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status).
- Checkout keeps working for every cart, whatever products have been deleted before.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} for a deleted product gives HTTP 404 Not Found. Deleting a product changes nothing about any other product.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.

findings.problem: The added test exercises OrderService directly and never calls the required merchant/customer order detail or list endpoints. It also does not assert the serialized product name, subtotal, unchanged order totals, or HTTP status-update endpoint behavior.
findings.impact: A defect in any of GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}, GET /api/v1/private/orders, GET /api/v1/auth/orders/{id}, GET /api/v1/auth/orders, or PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status could pass this test. No GitHub checks provide independent proof.
findings.correction: Add enabled HTTP integration coverage for all four retrieval endpoints and the status PUT after deletion, asserting SKU, name, quantity, price, subtotal, and unchanged totals; run and report it at this exact head.

findings.problem: The change contains no regression coverage for the cart lifecycle, checkout, deleted-SKU 404 behavior, v2 product 404 behavior, or preservation of another product.
findings.impact: The central cart and catalog acceptance requirements remain unverified, including empty-cart GET/PUT/multi behavior and ensuring deleted products are never ordered or charged.
findings.correction: Add integration tests that create carts with surviving and deleted products, exercise GET/PUT/multi/checkout, verify empty and recalculated totals, assert deleted-SKU 404 responses for cart addition and /api/v2/product/{sku}, and verify another product remains retrievable.

runs.report:
## Scope and repository confirmation
This checkout is Shopizer, a Maven multi-module Java platform. The requested endpoints and behavior are implemented in this repository. No GitHub issue was linked, and no repository label catalog was supplied, so no label suggestions are included. Working tree was clean and remains unmodified.

## Findings and evidence
- Product deletion is exposed by `sm-shop/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/shop/store/api/v1/product/ProductApi.java:164-171` and delegates to `ProductCommonFacadeImpl.deleteProduct`, which calls `ProductService.delete` (`sm-shop/.../ProductCommonFacadeImpl.java:388-408`).
- Cart lines do not have a persistent product foreign-key association: `ShoppingCartItem` stores `PRODUCT_ID` only as a scalar plus SKU, while its `Product` reference is `@Transient` (`sm-core-model/src/main/java/com/salesmanager/core/model/shoppingcart/ShoppingCartItem.java`). This should allow product deletion without deleting cart rows.
- Cart hydration resolves each line by SKU in `ShoppingCartServiceImpl.getPopulatedItem` (`sm-core/.../ShoppingCartServiceImpl.java:292-303`). Missing products are currently marked obsolete, but `getPopulatedShoppingCart` leaves them in the line-item set and marks the cart obsolete (`:230-264`). `getByCode` then deletes and returns `null` for an obsolete cart (`:182-198`), explaining both the broken-cart behavior and the empty-cart requirement failure.
- `ShoppingCartDataPopulator` dereferences `item.getProduct()` while constructing the response (`sm-shop/.../ShoppingCartDataPopulator.java:96-130`), so deleted lines must be removed before population. Totals and quantity are calculated from hydrated lines (`:174+` and the calculation service).
- Add-to-cart paths already reject a missing SKU, but one path throws a generic exception while the persistable API path uses `ResourceNotFoundException` (`ShoppingCartFacadeImpl.java:192-205`, `:250-273`, `:343-360`). The endpoint contract needs consistent HTTP 404 behavior for both single and multi-item additions.
- Checkout/shipping code iterates hydrated cart products (`ShoppingCartServiceImpl.java:369-384`), so pruning deleted lines before checkout is necessary to ensure deleted products are neither ordered nor charged.
- Order products are immutable snapshots: `OrderProduct` persists SKU, name, quantity, and one-time charge (`sm-core-model/.../OrderProduct.java`). `ReadableOrderProductMapper` copies those fields and only enriches the optional current product when it still exists (`sm-shop/.../ReadableOrderProductMapper.java:63-114`). This is compatible with deleted products, but all order retrieval paths and their fetch queries must be regression-tested.
- Merchant order retrieval uses `OrderRepository.findOne` with order-product fetches (`sm-core/.../OrderRepository.java:10-20`); no product join is present. Customer and merchant endpoints are in `sm-shop/.../OrderApi.java:220-310`, and status update is at `:494+`.
- V2 product lookup delegates directly to `getProductByCode` (`sm-shop/.../ProductApiV2.java:338-353`), which calls `ProductService.getBySku`; after deletion it should resolve to the existing not-found handling, but this endpoint needs an explicit regression check.

## Problem and proposed scope
Implement cart cleanup during hydration: remove missing-product lines and their orphaned cart attributes from the persisted/in-memory cart, retain the cart even when no lines remain, and calculate zero totals/quantity for an empty result. Ensure all cart mutation and checkout paths tolerate an empty cart and consistently return 404 when a requested product SKU no longer exists. Preserve order snapshot fields and avoid requiring a live catalog product for order serialization, retrieval, or status updates. Add focused integration coverage rather than changing product deletion semantics or order data.

## Acceptance checks
1. Create a cart with surviving and soon-to-be-deleted products, delete one, then GET `/api/v1/cart/{code}`: HTTP 200, deleted line absent, surviving totals and quantity correct.
2. Delete the only cart product: GET returns HTTP 200 with an empty product list, quantity 0, subtotal 0, total 0; the cart remains addressable.
3. PUT `/api/v1/cart/{code}` and POST `/api/v1/cart/{code}/multi` can remove/update/add surviving products after cleanup; attempts to add the deleted SKU return HTTP 404.
4. Checkout succeeds for carts containing stale deleted lines and creates no order line or charge for those products.
5. Deleted-product carts do not cause null dereferences in response mapping, pricing, shipping, or checkout.
6. After ordering, delete the catalog product and verify merchant detail/list and customer detail/list endpoints all return 200 and retain SKU, name, quantity, price, subtotal, and unchanged order totals.
7. Verify PUT `/api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status` still succeeds after product deletion.
8. Verify GET `/api/v2/product/{sku}` returns 404 for the deleted SKU and another product remains unchanged and retrievable.

## Likely affected components
- `sm-core` shopping-cart service and calculation/checkout integration.
- `sm-shop` cart facade, cart response populator/mapper, and v1 cart integration tests.
- `sm-shop` order facade/mapper only if a retrieval path still requires a live product; order API integration tests should cover all four read endpoints and status mutation.
- Product API v2 not-found regression test; product deletion implementation likely needs no behavioral redesign.

## Complexity and assumptions
Medium complexity: persistence is already SKU/scalar-based and orders already snapshot purchase data, but cart cleanup must be made safe across read, mutation, and checkout flows. Assumption: the existing test fixture infrastructure in `ServicesTestSupport` can create products, carts, and orders; if authenticated order fixtures are unavailable, add the smallest repository-consistent setup. No explicit design approval is required; acceptance behavior is concrete and implementation choices are already constrained by the existing service architecture.

## Existing tests and verification guidance
Existing cart integration coverage is in `sm-shop/src/test/java/com/salesmanager/test/shop/integration/cart/ShoppingCartAPIIntegrationTest.java`; it already exercises create, PUT, multi-update, and 404 cart paths. Order integration coverage is currently skeletal/ignored in `OrderApiIntegrationTest.java`, so new regression coverage will likely be needed for the order endpoints and deletion lifecycle. Run focused `sm-shop` tests, then the relevant Maven module test/build checks.

Task input (untrusted data):
<task>
You are working in a checkout of shopizer, a Java e-commerce platform (Maven, several modules; JDK 21 is installed and JAVA_HOME is set).

Merchants delete discontinued products all the time, and every time they do, something breaks. A cart that held the product can't be opened any more, and an order that included it can't be read by the merchant or by the customer who placed it.

Deleting a product (DELETE /api/v1/private/product/{id}) must not break carts or orders:

- Carts that held the product: GET /api/v1/cart/{code} returns the cart without it, with its subtotal, total and quantity worked out from the products left. A cart whose only product was deleted is returned with no products and a total of 0. The cart can still be changed (PUT /api/v1/cart/{code}, POST /api/v1/cart/{code}/multi) and checked out; the deleted product is never ordered or charged. Trying to add the deleted product to a cart gives HTTP 404 Not Found.
- Orders that included the product: GET /api/v1/private/orders/{id}, GET /api/v1/private/orders, GET /api/v1/auth/orders/{id} and GET /api/v1/auth/orders keep working, and show the product as it was bought: its sku, name, ordered quantity, price and subtotal, exactly as before it was deleted. The order's totals don't change. The order's status can still be changed (PUT /api/v1/private/orders/{id}/status).
- Checkout keeps working for every cart, whatever products have been deleted before.
- GET /api/v2/product/{sku} for a deleted product gives HTTP 404 Not Found. Deleting a product changes nothing about any other product.

When you have finished, reply with one short paragraph saying what you changed.
</task>
